# Use Alexa+ to Pick Up Common Phrases in Another Language

**Hook:** By the end of this guide, you'll know how to ask your Amazon Echo device for a translated phrase, hear it spoken out loud, and have a short back-and-forth to try it for yourself. This is for complete beginners who want a low-pressure way to dip into a new language at home. Honest note up front: **Alexa+** (Amazon's AI-powered upgrade to the standard Alexa assistant) isn't a dedicated language tutor. It won't grade your accent or run a structured lesson, but it IS great for quick translations, examples and casual practice you can fit into a normal day.

## Before you start
- An **Amazon Echo device** (such as an Echo Dot or Echo Show) that's already set up and connected to your home Wi-Fi.
- **Alexa+ enabled on your account.** Amazon currently offers Alexa+ to a limited set of users. If you're not sure whether you have it, ask your device *"Alexa, what's new with you?"* — a more chatty, natural-sounding reply suggests Alexa+ is on; a more scripted reply suggests the older version.
- A **language in mind** to practise. This guide uses **Spanish** as the example, but the same approach works for French, German, Italian, Japanese and many others.
- A quiet room so the microphone can pick you up clearly, and around **10 minutes** for a first practice session.

## Step 1 — Wake Alexa+ and ask for a phrase
Say the wake word out loud — **"Alexa…"** — followed by your request in plain English. There's no special "language mode" to open; you just talk to Alexa+ the way you'd talk to a helpful friend. The light ring on top of your Echo turns blue (or a small listening animation appears on an Echo Show screen) to show it's heard you. **If it looks different:** on Echo Show devices, a thin Alexa bar may slide up from the bottom of the screen with what you said written on it. If your device only answers in the old, more scripted Alexa style, the Alexa+ upgrade may not yet be active on your account — check Amazon's help pages for the latest rollout details.
💬 Example: say *"Alexa, how do I say 'where is the bathroom?' in Spanish?"*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ speaks the translated phrase out loud and usually adds a short English explanation alongside it.

## Step 2 — Ask for an example sentence and a slower version
Once you've heard the phrase, ask Alexa+ to put it into a short example sentence, and then ask it to slow down so you can really hear how each word sounds. This is where the conversational style of Alexa+ helps — you can keep asking follow-up questions in plain English without starting over. **If it looks different:** if Alexa+ speaks too fast on the first try, simply ask again and add *"slower, please"*. If it gives a very short answer and stops, just keep the conversation going with another question; there's no need to begin again from scratch.
💬 Example: say *"Can you use that in a short example sentence? And could you say it more slowly?"*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ repeats the phrase at a noticeably slower pace and gives you a sample sentence you could imagine using in a real situation.

## Step 3 — Repeat the phrase out loud and ask for the spelling
Now it's your turn. Say the phrase back out loud, even if it feels a little awkward at first. Then ask Alexa+ to spell it out letter by letter, so you can scribble it down in a notebook if you'd like to remember it later. **If it looks different:** on Echo Show devices, the phrase may already appear on screen alongside what you said — handy if you're a visual learner. If Alexa+ doesn't catch your voice clearly, move a step closer to the device and try again; background noise (kitchen fans, loud music) can confuse the microphone.
💬 Example: say *"Alexa, can you spell that phrase for me? I'd like to write it down."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ reads the phrase one letter at a time and you can copy it into a notebook without having to guess.

## Step 4 — Try a short back-and-forth before going all-in
Before jumping into a full conversation in another language, ask Alexa+ to walk you through how a real exchange would go — first in English, then in Spanish, side by side. This is a low-stakes way to rehearse a scenario like ordering coffee or asking for directions. **If it looks different:** if Alexa+ gives you a single sentence and stops, prompt it with *"what would they say back to me?"* — it usually continues the mini-dialogue. Be aware that Alexa+ isn't built as a role-play tutor, so the conversation may feel a little bumpy; treat it as practice, not a polished lesson, and don't worry about mistakes.
💬 Example: say *"Could we walk through ordering a coffee in Spanish? Show me what I would say, then what the barista would say back."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ gives you both sides of a small exchange, line by line, in both languages, and you can repeat each line back to yourself.

## Step 5 — Wrap up and save your favourite phrases
When you're ready to stop, simply say *"Alexa, stop"* or *"Alexa, that's all, thanks"*. Then grab a small notebook (or your phone's notes app) and write down two or three phrases you'd like to remember. Alexa+ doesn't currently keep a personal "phrases I've learned" list for you, so writing things down yourself is the most reliable way to remember them. **If it looks different:** if you'd like a refresher tomorrow, ask Alexa+ to **set a reminder** for a specific time — it will ping you out loud when the moment arrives. A paid Alexa+ plan, if your account has one, may add extra features over time, but the basic asking-and-listening flow above is what most people can use today.
💬 Example: say *"Thanks! Please set a reminder for tomorrow at 6pm to practise my Spanish phrases again."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ confirms the reminder out loud and the light ring returns to its usual idle colour.

## Common mistakes
- **Treating Alexa+ like a structured language course.** Alexa+ doesn't run lessons with levels, quizzes or progress tracking — it's a general AI helper. Use it for quick look-ups and casual practice, not a full curriculum.
- **Speaking too quietly or mumbling.** The far-field microphone works well, but it struggles in noisy kitchens. Stand about a metre away, face the device, and pause for a full second after each sentence.
- **Expecting perfect pronunciation feedback.** Alexa+ will happily repeat phrases slowly, but it won't grade your accent the way a human tutor would. Use it for rhythm and confidence, not as the final word on how you sound.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** a five-minute session each morning while the kettle boils is enough to pick up a handful of useful phrases in a week — no app switching, no screens, just talking to a small speaker on your bench.
- **For your business or work:** if you have clients or colleagues who speak another language, a quick daily session with Alexa+ can help you learn polite greetings and key questions before a trip or meeting, without needing to install a new app.
- **If you're just getting started:** the very easiest first move is to spend two minutes learning just three phrases — hello, thank you, and goodbye — in whichever language you've always been curious about.

## Try it now
In the next two minutes, walk over to your Echo device and say: **"Alexa, how do I say 'thank you very much' in Japanese, and could you say it slowly?"** Listen to the reply, repeat it once out loud, and you're already on your way.
